resources.string: Nothing pending. Add a weekly or daily alarm, a countdown, a monthly notice, or a flexible / one-off with +.

Needs you first, then the next 48 hours, then weekly / monthly. Add your own weekly or daily post with + and pick the days and time. Countdowns and daily posts are one card each. Tokens like {theme} come from Caption variables and fill in every caption.
No drafts yet. Open a task or start a blank caption.
Add fellowship members and OmniPost will nag you at 7:00 AM on the day.
Swipe right to see the other caption. Rotate the phone to see both at once.
Instagram letters copied. Paste into the caption box.
Any caption, not only a scheduled post
Paste WhatsApp markup or already-styled letters. *stars* become Instagram bold. _underscores_ stay italic. *_both_* is bold italic. Use Back to * _ to recover normal markup.
Caption saved. Next ring is 1 minute before post, then at post time — not 30 minutes early to write.
Flexible — not every week; I will set the next time
Pick a time in the future.
Post added. Write the caption yourself — OmniPost will shake you when it is time.
Brought back. OmniPost will nag until you post.
Write the caption and save it. Do not use a canned line — this post needs your words.
Write the caption, save it, then post when it is ready. OmniPost will keep coming until you mark Posted.
Nothing due right now. OmniPost is watching.
You write every caption. Writing gets a short vibrate. Sending the flyer uses the loud ring, plus a 1-minute warning so it goes out on time.
Vibrating. Tap an action now, or it will ring in 30 seconds.
Ringing for 5 minutes. Tap an action to stop.
Vibrate first. If you do not tap Open caption, I posted it, or Flyer not ready, it rings for 5 minutes so you cannot miss it.
A nudge to write the caption — not the loud ring. That is for sending the flyer, plus a 1-minute warning so it goes out on time.
One minute. Send it now so it goes out on time.
Off by default. You write the caption. Countdowns and monthly notices always fill from their template. Turn on only if you want canned lines for the weeklies.
Keeps OmniPost alive and refreshes the next item every minute, even after you leave. Leave this on for this phone.
Pops over the lock screen when it is time to write or post.
Uninstall wipes this phone. Export the desk to Drive or Downloads first — alarm settings, repeating posts, caption variables, birthdays, and drafts. Import that same file after you reinstall.
Desk saved. Keep that file off this phone so uninstall cannot take it.
Could not write the file. Try Drive or Downloads.
This replaces alarm settings, repeating posts, caption variables, birthdays, and drafts with the backup. Continue?
That file is not an OmniPost backup.
Weekly — pick days and the post time
Daily — every day at the time you pick

Sunday Service is already weekly. Add more weeklies or a daily post and choose the days and the exact time. Countdowns and monthly notices still live here. Caption variables work in every post. Long-press a card on Tasks to edit.
Extra tokens for this post only (optional, one per line: name=value)

Inbuilt: {today} {date} {weekday} {month} {year} {start} {end} {range} {Days} {away} {days} {name} {now} {clock}. {date} is the due day; {today} is today. Nested: {range:today:date} {today+3}. Caption variables work in every caption.
Pick last day (fills the range token)
Daily until D-Day — one card, day count updates itself
Last day of previous month, then the 10th and 20th — month name updates itself
Weekly — choose the days and the post time
Daily — every day at the post time, one card on the desk
Rings every day at the time below. The desk keeps one card so days do not pile up. {weekday} and {date} fill themselves.
Tokens you can drop into any caption
Inbuilt tokens are listed first. Yours can use them: write {today}, {date}, {theme}, or {range:today:date} inside another variable. {date} is when the post is due; {today} is today.
Inbuilt tokens are listed above. Tap + to add your own.
Name is the token. Value may use other tokens — {today}, {date}, {theme}, {range:start:end}, {today+3}. The preview fills them live.
Value — as long as you need
Pick a token name to preview {name}.
Use letters, then letters, numbers, or underscore. No spaces.
That name is inbuilt. Pick another, or use it inside the value.
A range depends on two dates: {range:today:date}, {range:start:end}, {range:today:today+6}. Offsets: {today+3} {date-1}.
Insert range from today to due date
That token name is already in use.
Variable saved. Use it as {name} in any caption.
%1$s will no longer fill in captions. The words you already wrote stay as they are.
Last day of the previous month
Pick at least one date in the month.
Repeating post saved. OmniPost will nag you to write the caption.
“%1$s” will leave the desk. It will not come back on its own.

OmniPost must appear under Special app access → Alarms & reminders. Grant every row. Keep-alive is optional: it does not read your screen; it only stops this phone from burying the desk. Then run the 70-second test and swipe the app away.
OmniPost uses this only to stay running so posting alarms still fire after you leave. It does not read your screen, passwords, or other apps, and it does not tap anything.
Also enable Autostart and set App battery manager → OmniPost → Unrestricted. Without that, swipe-away still kills alarms on many African OEMs.
WhatsApp is not installed. Caption copied to the clipboard.
Copied. Pick the Important Info group in WhatsApp.
Draft in 5s, then the nag. Swipe OmniPost away to prove it.
Final post — as it will look
Upcoming birthday tasks for %1$s will be cancelled.
If this is not posted, OmniPost will keep coming back. If the flyer is not ready, tell it when to nag again. Change the interval in Settings.
%1$d task(s) still not marked Posted. OmniPost will not go quiet.
Caption-ready window. Write it, save it, then post when it is time.
Draft and post the birthday greeting by 7:00 AM.
Post that New Month Fasting starts tomorrow.
Post the fasting reminder again on the day itself.
Draft and post the Happy New Month caption for the 1st.
